rungs.title: Divisor–Chern identity as an exact equality on the pinned cycle class: the class of a Cartier divisor D equals the rational image of c₁(𝒪(D)), sign determined
rungs.note: Checked at this repository's pin in the port (2026-11-24). Statement (upstream's HasDivisorClassOfCartierData, as defined at the pin): for every invertible sheaf L, unit extension E with L^an ≅ its section sheaf, and Cartier datum c representing L, sheafCycleClassOnCycles 1 c.divisor = integralToRationalCohomology 2 E.firstChernClass, with sign +. sheafCycleClassOnCycles is upstream main's (Other/AlgebraicGeometry/Cycle/SheafClass.lean), built from main's cycleComponentSheafClass, the class of record; no copy is staged. Exactness on main's class comes from the port's bridge cycleComponentSheafClass_eq_injectiveModel (no scalar) and the transport of the normalization (componentTransport). Signs met on the way are in docs/conventions.md (orientation against winding +1, kernel-checked).

rungs.title: Rational first Chern classes and Cartier divisor classes are Hodge classes; F¹ is the kernel of the projection to 𝒪
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-24. Ω⁰ ≅ 𝒪; the stupid truncation 0 → F¹Ω^• → Ω^• → 𝒪[0] → 0 is short exact, so F¹ H^n_dR is exactly the kernel of H^n_dR → ℍ^n(𝒪[0]) (both inclusions); conjugation fixes de Rham images of rational classes. Hence the rational image of an integral degree-two class is a Hodge class iff it vanishes in H²(𝒪); first Chern classes do (exponential sequence), and so do classes of divisors of Cartier data (divisor–Chern, sign +). This is the known half in codimension one for Cartier divisors.

rungs.title: Unique factorization descends along faithfully flat local homomorphisms from a Noetherian local domain to a local UFD
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25 (Mori's descent, local case). Height-one prime P, 0 ≠ a ∈ P: the double colon (aA : (aA : P)) extends to a principal ideal of B (flat base change of colons by the equational criterion; double colons are principal in a UFD), descends to tA (faithful flatness), and equals P (P is associated to A/aA; Nakayama). Mathlib candidate.

rungs.title: The ideal sheaf of a prime divisor is an invertible sheaf represented by Cartier data whose divisor is minus the prime divisor
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. On a smooth projective integral complex scheme, the vanishing ideal sheaf of every prime divisor D = closure {ξ} is invertible (Tau Ceti IsInvertible) and is represented by Cartier data with divisor −D. Route: the vanishing ideal sheaf as S.Modules (HodgeLadder.Divisor.IdealSheaf); near each closed point of D a local equation π (height-one prime of the UFD local ring, principal after inverting one element on an affine open: HeightOneGenerator, LocalGenerator), and 1 away from D; local generation gives generating sections (generates_of_dividesVanishingAt) and hence invertibility (Tau Ceti ofClosedPoints); ord π = 1 at ξ and 0 at other codimension-one points (Mathlib's Scheme.ord), so the Cartier data with local equations π⁻¹ have divisor −D. Sign: the ideal sheaf is 𝒪(−D), so the divisor is −D; −[D] Hodge gives [D] Hodge.

rungs.title: Every invertible sheaf has a unit extension E with L^an ≅ E.sectionSheafOfModules
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For invertible L on a smooth projective integral complex scheme, L^an is invertible (coherent by Oka, stalks free of rank one, X(ℂ) T1 hence Jacobson; Tau Ceti's closed-point criterion), so it has holomorphic frames σᵢ with σᵢ = gᵢⱼ • σⱼ. The middle sheaf N has sections (n, v) with n locally constant and g(b·)ᵢ·^n · v holomorphic on each Uᵢ (a local predicate); 0 → 𝒪ˣ → N → ℤ → 0 is short exact, with ℤ identified with locally constant functions (constIsoLC). E's chosen lifts of 1 have degree one and transitionUnit y x = vʸ/vˣ; the frames wˣᵢ • σᵢ (wˣᵢ = g(b·)ᵢ · vˣ) on the cover Oₓ ⊓ Uᵢ have E's transitions, and Frames.isoOfSameTransitions gives L^an ≅ E.section. This route does not use the stack's AnalytificationGenerates. Convention: docs/conventions.md, row 'Unit extension of a line bundle'.

rungs.title: Assembly: every prime divisor class is a Hodge class (CycleClassesAreHodgeOne)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For a prime divisor D = closure {ξ}: the ideal sheaf is invertible with Cartier data of divisor −D (prime-divisor-ideal-sheaf), its analytification is E.section for a unit extension E (unit-extension-of-invertible), so sheafCycleClassOnCycles 1 (single ξ (−1)) = −[D] is Hodge (chern-classes-are-hodge) and [D] is Hodge. The classes of prime divisors span algebraicCycleClassSpan X 1 (sSup of spans).

rungs.title: Lefschetz (1,1) as an equality: theorem : HodgeLadder.LefschetzOneOneEquality
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25: theorem lefschetzOneOneEquality_holds : HodgeLadder.LefschetzOneOneEquality, from lefschetzOneOneEquality_iff with lefschetzOneOne_holds (upstream inclusion, ported) and cycleClassesAreHodgeOne_holds (prime-divisors-cartier). The checkpoint's definition of done (decision 0004). Red team: pass with changes (docs/sketches/lefschetz-1-1-equality.redteam.md). Non-vacuity in degree two: projective-line-test (checked), where both sides are one-dimensional.

rungs.title: Prove the known half: theorem : HodgeLadder.CycleClassesAreHodge
rungs.note: The known half of the conjecture. With it, the upstream HodgeConjecture is equivalent to the equality Hdg^p = span, and the statement cannot hold for a degenerate reason (span accidentally everything). Classical route: a Hodge-cohomology cycle class (El Zein; Voisin2002 ch. 11) comparing cohomology with support in Z of the truncated de Rham complex with the topological class. Large; p = 1 comes first through lefschetz-1-1-equality.

rungs.title: Integral Lefschetz (1,1): the image of c₁ : Pic(X) → H²(X(ℂ); ℤ) equals the integral classes whose rational image is a Hodge class
rungs.note: The literature's form of the theorem (Lefschetz1924, GriffithsHarris1978). Upstream's proof deliberately stops at the rational span. Both inclusions are needed; torsion classes are in the image because they lie in the kernel of H²(ℤ) → H²(𝒪). Integral HC fails in higher codimension (problem.md §2), so this is the one codimension where the integral equality holds.

rungs.title: Computed test case: for projective space ℙ^n over ℂ (n ≥ 1), Hdg^1 = algebraicCycleClassSpan 1, and both are one-dimensional over ℚ
rungs.note: Pins the definitions from both sides at once: a nonzero class in degree 2, a nonzero hyperplane class, and no room for a degenerate reading. Inventory 2026-11-25 (docs/sketches/projective-space-test.md): nothing at the pin computes H² of a positive-dimensional X, and Mathlib has no smoothness or integrality of Proj. Split into sub-rungs on ℙ¹: projective-line-witness, projective-line-point, forget-support-exact (checked), contractible-open-acyclic, projective-line-class-nonzero, projective-line-h2, projective-line-test. This rung keeps the ℙⁿ statement (n ≥ 1); the ℙ¹ case is posted separately as projective-line-test. The hyperplane-class sign is a conventions-register row. The ℙ¹ case (projective-line-test) is checked 2026-11-25; the ℙⁿ statement for n ≥ 2 stays open.

rungs.title: ℙ¹ over ℂ in upstream's sense (ProjectiveSpace.toBase (Fin 2) (Spec ℂ) as X : Over (Spec ↧ℂ)) is integral, smooth of relative dimension one and projective
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Smooth of relative dimension one: Oka's standard charts of ℙₒ(n; R) are Spec R[Y₁..Yₙ], standard smooth of relative dimension n (Mathlib), and upstream's structure morphism is a base change of ℙₒ(1; ULift ℤ) → Spec (ULift ℤ). rungs.title: ℙ¹ has a point x of coheight one whose analytic support has contractible complement (homeomorphic to ℂ)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. The point [1 : 0] is the complement of the chart X₁ ≠ 0 (in the chart X₀ ≠ 0 it is the only prime of ℂ[Y] containing Y), so it is closed of coheight one; the chart is affine space over Spec ℂ, and upstream's affineSpaceHomeomorph gives a homeomorphism of the support complement with ℂ.

rungs.title: Forgetting support is injective in degree n + 1 and surjective in degree n when H^n of the open complement vanishes
rungs.note: Exactness of the long exact sequence of the pair (X(ℂ), X(ℂ) ∖ Z) at H_[Z]^{n+1} and at H^n, read off Mathlib's contravariant Ext sequence for upstream's pair sheaf (Sheaf.pairShortComplex_shortExact). The hypothesis is on Sheaf.H' of the constant sheaf ℚ over the open complement; no property of X is used.

rungs.title: For smooth projective integral X over ℂ and a contractible open U ⊆ X(ℂ), Sheaf.H' of the constant sheaf ℚ over U vanishes in positive degrees
rungs.note: Flasque-resolution argument on the open itself, no open-subscheme detour: Sheaf.H' over U is H^q(U, ℚ_X|_U) (Oka H'AddEquiv), ℚ_X|_U ≅ ℚ_U (inverse image commutes with constant sheaves). On a contractible Hausdorff space Y with paracompact opens and a contractible open basis, ℚ_Y → 𝒞^•(Y) (sheafified singular cochains) is a flasque resolution whose global sections are exact in positive degrees (upstream quasi-isomorphisms plus singularCochainComplex_exactAt_of_contractible); flasque sheaves are acyclic and dimension shifting along the cycle sheaves gives H^{q+1}(Y; ℚ) = 0. The topological statement subsingleton_H_const_of_contractible uses no algebraic geometry; X enters only through T2, paracompact opens and exists_contractibleOpen_le. Composes with forgetSupport_injective_of_subsingleton.

rungs.title: The class of a point of ℙ¹ is nonzero in H²(ℙ¹; ℚ), so algebraicCycleClassSpan ℙ¹ 1 ≠ ⊥
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. General criterion (any smooth projective X, codimension one): the class is nonzero when H¹ of the support complement vanishes, from upstream's nonzero supported class (normalization isomorphism) and forget-support-exact. On ℙ¹ the complement of [1 : 0] is contractible (projective-line-point), hence acyclic (contractible-open-acyclic).

rungs.title: H²(ℙ¹; ℚ) is one-dimensional and equals algebraicCycleClassSpan ℙ¹ 1
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For a curve and a point with acyclic complement, forgetting support is bijective in degree two; upstream identifies H_[Z]²(X; ℚ) with relative singular cohomology H²(X(ℂ), X(ℂ) ∖ {p}; ℚ), which is spanned by the nonzero local coclass (span_analyticPointLocalCoclass_eq_top), so H² has rank one; the nonzero point class then spans it.

rungs.title: Computed test case on ℙ¹: Hdg^1(ℙ¹; ℚ) = algebraicCycleClassSpan ℙ¹ 1, and both are one-dimensional over ℚ
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Hdg^1(ℙ¹; ℚ) = algebraicCycleClassSpan ℙ¹ 1 is lefschetzOneOneEquality_holds at ℙ¹; both are H²(ℙ¹; ℚ), of rank one (projective-line-h2). This is the degree-two non-vacuity test for lefschetz-1-1-equality (red-team finding on that rung).

rungs.title: The Clifford algebra of the split form on H ⊕ H^∨ acts on the exterior algebra ∧*H as its spin module, compatible with parity
rungs.note: Research note 2026-11-24 §1. For a torus A with H = H¹(A, ℚ), H*(A, ℚ) = ∧*H, so Spin(H ⊕ H^∨) acts on all of H*(A, ℚ) (Chevalley1954, Mukai1981); Markman's Weil-class construction uses this action through Orlov's equivalence. Pure linear algebra over Mathlib's CliffordAlgebra and ExteriorAlgebra; a Mathlib upstream candidate. Sequenced after the Lefschetz checkpoint.

rungs.title: Computed test: for elliptic curves E₁, E₂, dim Hdg^1(E₁ × E₂; ℚ) = 2 + rank Hom(E₁, E₂), while h^{1,1} = 4
rungs.note: Research note 2026-11-24 §3. Shows on upstream definitions that Hodge classes depend on the periods, not the Hodge diamond (dimension 2, 3 or 4). Also checks the Hodge numbers of products of elliptic curves against the refined Künneth count. Needs the cohomology of tori on upstream definitions.

rungs.title: Front cup: a ring structure on upstream's rational cohomology
rungs.note: Decision 0008. Yoneda route: H^n(X; ℚ) ≅ Ext^n(ℚ_X, ℚ_X) in sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces, product = Ext.comp. Kill criterion: no compatibility with the cycle class map. Blocks the Markman inventory's degree-four list and M3. Amended by decision 0009: comparison with the singular cup product is an explicit rung (cup-singular-comparison), and the kill criterion includes fixing its sign.

rungs.title: H^n(X; ℚ) ≅ Ext^n(ℚ_X, ℚ_X) in sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces on X(ℂ)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For any topological space Y: forgetting the ℚ-structure of sheaves is exact (left exact as a right adjoint; preserves epimorphisms since they are the locally surjective maps), sheafified ℚ ⊗ − is exact (ℚ flat over ℤ; whiskering and sheafification left exact), so Adjunction.extEquiv applies; sheafified ℚ ⊗ − sends ℤ_Y to ℚ_Y (uniqueness of left adjoints to global sections) and forgetting sends ℚ_Y to ℚ_Y (constantCommuteCompose). Hence Hⁿ(Y; ℚ) ≃+ Extⁿ(ℚ_Y, ℚ_Y) in sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces.

rungs.title: Cup product on H^*(X; ℚ): definition, associativity, unit, bilinearity
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. α ∪ β is the Yoneda composition of α followed by β in Ext^*(ℚ_X, ℚ_X) (convention row 'Cup product'); the target degree carries a proof of p + q = n. Associative, unital, biadditive. Non-vacuity: on ℙ¹, 1 ∪ [pt] = [pt] ≠ 0 (HodgeLadder.Tests.projectiveLine_one_cup_ne_zero, module HodgeLadder.Tests.CupNonvanishing). Graded commutativity and comparison with the topological cup product are open (cup-graded-commutative). Vacuity gap: these laws also hold for the square-zero product; cup-positive-degree-test closes it.

rungs.title: Pullback along a morphism of complex schemes on H^*(X; ℚ) is multiplicative for the cup product
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For a continuous map f, the inverse image f⁻¹ of sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces is exact (representably flat for finite limits; left adjoint) and f⁻¹ ℚ_X ≅ ℚ_Y (uniqueness of left adjoints to global sections); conjugating Ext classes by an exact functor is multiplicative and unital (conjExt_comp, conjExt_id). For g : X' ⟶ X over Spec ℂ, pullbackCoh g is additive, multiplicative and sends 1 to 1. Open: agreement with the port's abelian-group pullback TopCat.Sheaf.H.pullback, and functoriality in g.

rungs.title: The tensor product of sheaves of ℚ-vector spaces on X(ℂ) is exact in each variable
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Monoidal structure: Mathlib Sheaf.monoidalCategory (localization of the pointwise presheaf tensor along sheafification) as the local instance HodgeLadder.Cup.sheafMonoidal, braiding Sheaf.braidedCategory. Stated for any Y : TopCat.{0} with J Y = Opens.grothendieckTopology Y, so it applies to X(ℂ). For every sheaf F, tensorLeft F and tensorRight F preserve finite limits, finite colimits (indeed small colimits) and are additive (HodgeLadder.Cup.tensor_exact). Route: tensorLeft F ≅ forget ⋙ tensorLeft F.obj ⋙ sheafify; pointwise tensor over ℚ is flat; colimits via sheafification of the underlying presheaf diagram; tensorRight by the braiding. Unit: 𝟙_ ≅ ℚ_Y by Iso.refl (HodgeLadder.Cup.unitIsoQX). Mathlib candidate (decision 0009).

rungs.title: Product of a supported class in H_[Z]^p(X; ℚ) with an absolute class, compatible with forgetting the support
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. α ∪ β := α ≫ lift β, where lift β ∈ Ext^q(ℚ_X, ℚ_X) of abelian sheaves is the image of β under the exact forgetful functor, conjugated by forget ℚ_X ≅ ℚ_X. Composition with lift matches the cup product (rationalExtEquiv_comp_lift, from Mathlib's extEquiv_symm_naturality_right), so the product is associative with cup, unital, biadditive, natural in the source, and commutes with forgetting the support. The tensor product (sheaf-tensor-exact) is not needed here; it enters for products of two supported classes.

rungs.title: The cup product on upstream's singular cochains, through a cochain isomorphism with Tau Ceti's model
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Upstream's singular chain complex with ℚ coefficients is Tau Ceti's with unit coefficients (rfl); linear duals are morphisms into ℚ degreewise (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv), giving cohIso : Cohomology ℚ X n ≅ Tau Ceti's singular cohomology. cupSing is Tau Ceti's cup (front face times back face) transported; b ∪ a = (−1)^{pq} a ∪ b and associativity hold.

rungs.title: Right multiplication by a global cocycle as a morphism of complexes of sheaves on the sheafified singular cochains
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. For a global singular q-cocycle b, right multiplication c ↦ c ∪ b|_U (Tau Ceti cupCochain along the Alexander–Whitney diagonal of U) on upstream's singular cochain presheaves is natural under restriction (alexanderWhitneyDiagonal_naturality, cupCochain_naturality) and commutes with the coboundary in degrees n ↦ n + q (Leibniz rule, δb = 0); sheafified, it commutes with the sheaf coboundary. The shift sign (−1)^{nq} needed for a map into S•[q] is left to ext-class-right-mult.

rungs.title: Right multiplication by a global cocycle as a degree-q cocycle of the Hom complex Hom(S_ℤ, S_ℤ), components (−1)^{pq} r_p
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. On S_ℤ = S.extend embeddingUpNat, the Hom-complex cochain with components (−1)^{pq} · rightMulSheaf b in source degree p ≥ 0 and 0 below has δ = 0: the two terms of Mathlib's δ formula cancel by r ≫ d = d ≫ r and (−1)^{q+1}(−1)^{(p+1)q} = −(−1)^{pq}. Cocycle.equivHomShift gives the chain map rightMulHom : S_ℤ ⟶ S_ℤ⟦q⟧ with Mathlib's shift signs.

rungs.title: Right multiplication by a global cocycle b on upstream's constant cochains: ι⁰ ≫ r_b is the sheafification of r ↦ r · b|_U, and sends the constant global section 1 to b
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Upstream's zero-chain augmentation is Tau Ceti's constant cochain with value 1 (checked vertex by vertex); the left unit law cupCochain_constCochain_left gives (r·1) ∪ b|_U = r · b|_U; the identity passes to sheaves by functoriality of sheafification and to global sections by naturality of the unit. Restating this as a degree-q Hom-complex cocycle ℤ[0] → S_ℤ in upstream's integer-constant form is part of ext-class-right-mult, where upstream's step 2 is unfolded.

rungs.title: The derived-category class of a Hom-complex cocycle is compatible with pre- and postcomposition by chain maps
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. General abelian C, any universe w: toSmallShiftedHom (mk (z.postcomp g)) = (toSmallShiftedHom (mk z)).comp (mk₀ g), and the same for precomposition; from Cocycle.equivHomShift_symm_postcomp/precomp and ShiftedHom.map_comp. A Mathlib candidate (docs/gaps.md).

rungs.title: Upstream's step 2 sends the class of a Hom-complex cocycle z : ℤ[0] → S_ℤ to the homology class of the global section z names, for every K-injective resolution
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Unfolds rationalSingularCochainHypercohomologyAddEquivGlobalSectionsOfResolution stage by stage: cocycle-class-comp for the postcomposition with the resolution and the precomposition with the integer-constant isomorphism, equivOfIsKInjective on a class, upstream's homologyAddEquiv_postcompMap and homComplexSingleIntegerIsoGlobalSections_naturality (Other library), then the inverse of the global-sections quasi-isomorphism. The answer does not involve the resolution.

rungs.title: For a global q-cocycle b: R_b ∘ ι_ℤ is the Hom-complex cocycle ℤ_Y[0] → S_ℤ sending 1 to b, its derived-category class is ι_ℤ followed by the class of R_b, and upstream's step 2 sends it to the global-section class it names, for every K-injective resolution
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. ι_ℤ has degree-zero component ℤ_Y → ℚ_Y → S⁰ (mkHomFromSingle). The component of R_b ∘ ι_ℤ out of ℤ_Y is compared with the map 1 ↦ b by evaluation at 1 (integerConstantHomAddEquivGlobalSections is injective): ℤ_Y → ℚ_Y sends 1 to the sheafified constant 1 (adjunction unit), and right-mult-unit does the rest. The sign is (−1)^{0·q} = 1. With cocycle-class-comp and step2-cocycle-class this gives the step-2 image. The original form ι[q] ∘ ε([b]) = R_b ∘ ι follows by bijectivity of upstream's steps 1 and 2 once ι_ℤ is identified with upstream's ι (rung iota-upstream) and is stated inside cup-singular-comparison.

rungs.title: ι_ℤ composed with upstream's integer-constant isomorphism equals upstream's ℤ_X → ℚ_X followed by rationalToSingularCochainComplexInt
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Both sides are maps out of a single complex, so they agree once their degree-zero components do (from_single_hom_ext); extend_single_comp_f computes the extended side in degree zero for any abelian category, and both components are ℤ_X → ℚ_X → S⁰. iso_hom_iotaZ: upstream's integer-constant isomorphism followed by ι_ℤ is intToRatComplex followed by rationalToSingularCochainComplexInt.

rungs.title: The derived-category class of a composite of Hom-complex cocycles is the composite of their classes, with no sign
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. General abelian C. Cochain.comp and rightShift carry no sign, and the shift of a chain map has no sign, so equivHomShift.symm (z.comp w) = (equivHomShift.symm z).comp (equivHomShift.symm w) componentwise; ShiftedHom.map_comp passes to the derived category. A Mathlib candidate (docs/gaps.md).

rungs.title: The composite of the cocycle naming a with right multiplication by b is (−1)^{pq} times the cocycle naming a ∪ b
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Both sides are cocycles out of ℤ_Y[0], so they agree once their components out of ℤ_Y do (fromSingleEquiv). The component of the composite is the map 1 ↦ a followed by R_b in source degree p, which is (−1)^{pq} · rightMulSheaf b; evaluated at 1, right multiplication sends the sheafified a to the sheafified a ∪ b (naturality of sheafification). The sign (−1)^{pq} is exactly rightMulCochain's. The derived form follows from cocycle-class-mul.

rungs.title: The Yoneda cup product in sheaves of abelian groups: α ∪ β = α followed by forgetEnd(e β), the endomorphism class of ℚ_Y obtained by forgetting the ℚ-structure of e β; in particular β = 1 followed by forgetEnd(e β)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Ext algebra over Mathlib's Adjunction.extEquiv_symm_naturality_right for ℚ ⊗ − ⊣ forget: the forgetQX conjugations cancel and the adjunction moves y.mapExactFunctor forget past the transport. The second half of the original statement (the endomorphism class of [b], followed by ι, is ι followed by R_b) is the open rung end-class-right-mult.

rungs.title: ℚ ⊗ (ℤ_Y → ℚ_Y) is an isomorphism, and precomposition with ℤ_Y → ℚ_Y is injective on Ext^n(ℚ_Y, M) for every sheaf M of ℚ-vector spaces, in particular M = ℚ_Y
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. On abelian groups ℚ ⊗ κ is an isomorphism by the coyoneda criterion and the adjunction: an additive map from ℚ to a ℚ-vector space is q ↦ q • f(1) (map_rat_smul). On sheaves by naturality of tensorQConstIso. Cancellation by Adjunction.extEquiv_naturality_left₀.

rungs.title: The unit oneY of H^0(Y; ℚ) is the class of ℤ_Y → ℚ_Y, so every β is κ followed by its endomorphism class forgetEnd(e β)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Key identity: the adjoint of tensorQSheafInt followed by forgetQX is κ, compared through the constant-sheaf adjunction as maps ℤ → Γ(ℚ_Y). tensorQConstIso is read off by homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app; the unit of ℚ ⊗ − followed by ℚ ⊗ ℤ ≅ ℚ is the cast (elementwise, cancelling the counit of forget₂.asEquivalence); forgetQX sends sheafified constant sections to sheafified constant sections (sheafComposeIso_inv_fac and naturality of sheafification).

rungs.title: Mathlib's Ext classes between constant sheaves and upstream's Hypercohomology classes agree in the derived category of sheaves of abelian groups on X(ℂ), through single versus extended complexes and upstream's ULift identification
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Public restatement of upstream's private hypercohomologyAddEquivConstantCohomology_hom: in the derived category, the Ext class of α is α preceded by the inverse of the source comparison (constantIntegerSheafComplexIntIsoSingleULift) and followed by the target comparison (constantFieldSheafComplexIntIsoSingle). rungs.title: For β ∈ H^q(X; ℚ) that upstream's comparison (steps 1 and 2, any K-injective resolution) sends to the class named by a global cocycle b: forgetEnd(e β) followed by ι[q] equals ι followed by the class of R_b, in the derived category of sheaves of abelian groups on X(ℂ)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Step 2 is injective, so step 1 of β is the class of R_b ∘ ι_ℤ ∘ e, which is R_b precomposed with intToRatComplex ≫ ι (iota-upstream, cocycle level). In the derived category: ext-derived-bridge writes step 1 of β through β.hom, one-is-kappa writes β.hom = κ ≫ ε.hom, and the comparison square uliftIso_hom_kappa lines up both sides behind the isomorphism Q(e_A). Cancelling it, then Q(ι) (an isomorphism, ι a quasi-isomorphism), then κ (kappa_cancel_derived from kappa-cancel) leaves ε ≫ ι[q] = ι ≫ R_b. The algebra is isolated in end_class_core, stated in one spelling of the sheaf category.

rungs.title: If upstream's steps 1 and 2 send x ∈ H^p and y ∈ H^q to the global-section classes named by cocycles a and b, they send cup x y to (−1)^{pq} times the class named by a ∪ b (any K-injective resolution)
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. cup x y = x followed by forgetEnd(e y) (ab-ext-yoneda); the bridge for x and for the cup product, and end-class-right-mult for y, give step 1 of the cup as step 1 of x followed by the class of R_b. The shifted-hom algebra is shiftedHom_cup_core, proved in any category with a shift by ℤ. Then cocycle-class-mul and named-cocycle-comp turn [z_a].[R_b] into (−1)^{pq}[z_{a∪b}], and step 2 on cocycle classes finishes. The sign is the one predicted in the sketch.

rungs.title: Upstream's equivalence Ψ from rational sheaf cohomology to rational singular cohomology satisfies Ψ(x ∪ y) = (−1)^{pq} · cupSing (Ψ x) (Ψ y), same order
rungs.note: Checked 2026-11-25. Every singular class is singClass of a global cocycle (exists_singClass); step 3 is injective, so step 1 of x is the class named by its cocycle; cup-global-comparison for upstream's chosen resolution gives step 2 of the cup; step3-named-class and cup-top-open finish. Sign-free form: Ψ (x ∪ y) = cupSing (Ψ y) (Ψ x) (cup_singular_comparison_swap), since Mathlib's Ext.comp is diagrammatic. Red team: pass with changes (docs/sketches/cup-singular-comparison-absolute.redteam.md); the hypotheses hold on upstream's ℙ¹ (cup-comparison-projective-line). The sign is fixed by the kernel proof; no computed instance yet has a nonzero product of two positive-degree classes (cup-odd-degree-test, cup-positive-degree-test).

rungs.title: Markman's theorem as a solved-research statement on upstream definitions: Weil classes on abelian fourfolds of Weil type are algebraic
rungs.note: Front abelian. The Lefschetz checkpoint is checked and the inventory is written (docs/notes/2026-11-25-markman-inventory.md); blocked on front cup (decision 0008); first Markman-directed rung is the inventory's T1 (Weil classes on abelian surfaces of Weil type). Source Markman2025 is an unrefereed preprint (latest arXiv v2, 2025-06-08); its all-discriminant proof passes through Weil classes on sixfolds (degree six), and Voisin2026Bourbaki (Lemma 2.9, Cor 2.10) replaces Schoen's degeneration by a product reduction. Only the discriminant-1 route (Markman2023, refereed) stays in degree four. The statement records which source it rests on and the discriminant convention (docs/conventions.md). Markman's method produces a sheaf whose characteristic class must equal a given Weil class with exact normalization; the statement records the normalization.
